What you've already tried

You bought the licences. The work didn't change.

Most organisations have already spent on AI. The spend shows up in the budget. It rarely shows up in how long the monthly report takes.

The licence rollout

Seats for Copilot or ChatGPT, a launch email, a spike in logins. By week six the usage dashboard tells the real story.

The tool works. Nobody connected it to the work.

The lunch-and-learn

An inspiring hour on what AI can do. Everyone nods. Monday's board pack is built exactly the way it was last month.

Nobody connected the tool to the board pack.

The e-learning module

Forty minutes of generic video and a green tick in the LMS. Completion was measured. Capability wasn't.

The tool was taught. The documents were left alone.

The innovation pilot

One clever proof of concept in one team. It impressed ExCo, then never left the sandbox.

It connected the tool to a demo, not to the reports people produce every Monday.

The policy memo

AI restricted pending review. Meanwhile people paste company documents into personal accounts, because the deadline didn't wait.

The tool was locked. The risk walked right past it.

The difference

Built on your documents, not the tool's feature list.

Adoption stalls when training teaches the tool and leaves the work alone. We start from the other end.

The tool already works. What doesn't work is the gap between the tool and the document your person produces every Monday morning. A monthly report doesn't need someone who knows more AI features. It needs a method: a structured brief instead of a blank page, the right source material already summarised, the house style applied in seconds instead of hours. Close that gap and the tool does what the licence promised.

That gap is where we work.

Delivery

Workshops your people build in. Packs they keep.

  1. 01

    Baseline

    We time a sample of the documents each team produces today: monthly reports, proposals, board packs, client letters. That is the number we are measured against.

  2. 02

    Live workshops

    Presentation-style sessions, in the room or online, run team by team. Every person works on a real document from their own desk, not a demo on ours.

  3. 03

    Follow-along packs

    Each role gets a printed and digital pack to follow during the session and keep afterwards, so the method outlives the day.

  4. 04

    Measure and report

    Thirty days later we time the same documents again and report to the sponsor: hours returned, by team, in rand.

Questions

Questions sponsors ask first.

What does corporate AI training from GrowthCred include?+
A baseline of how long your teams take on their real documents, live workshop sessions run team by team, a follow-along pack for every role, and a measurement thirty days later reported to your sponsor in hours and rand.
How do you measure 3× faster?+
Before training we time a sample of real documents per team, at the review standard you already use. Thirty days after, we time the same kinds of document again. 3× is the target we train to; the report shows the measured number, whatever it is.
How is corporate AI training priced?+
Per employee trained. We quote after the baseline, so the fee is set against the capacity it returns. The number of people, teams and role-specific packs changes the quote.
Which AI tools do you train on?+
Whichever platform your organisation has approved, such as Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. The method stays the same; the packs are written for your tool.
Is the training in person or online?+
Either. Sessions run in the room in Johannesburg, or online for teams elsewhere in South Africa and abroad.
What about confidential information and POPIA?+
Practice uses redacted or fictional material, and every pack sets out what may never go into an AI tool. Training happens inside your approved, company-controlled accounts. Training alone does not make a workflow compliant; your policies and legal team still decide.
Do our people need to be technical?+
No. If they can write an email and work in a spreadsheet, they can do this. Every session is built around documents they already produce.
Is the training accredited?+
No. This is practical workplace training, not an accredited qualification, and no accreditation is claimed.
